study type: Experimental animal study (genetic engineering, in vitro cell analysis, in vivo pig generation)
exposure: Genetic modification of porcine P53 gene using TALENs and somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) to achieve biallelic knockout
outcome: Successful generation of P53 biallelic knockout (KO) Diannan miniature pig cell lines and live piglets
Confirmed P53 knockout and reduced mRNA expression in KO piglets
Defective DNA damage response in P53 KO fibroblast cells upon doxorubicin treatment
cohort: Diannan miniature pig fetal fibroblasts were used to establish cell lines, which then served as donors for somatic cell nuclear transfer to generate P53 KO Diannan miniature pig fetuses and live piglets.
finding: The study successfully generated P53 biallelic knockout Diannan miniature pigs via TALENs and SCNT, demonstrating dysfunctional P53 gene expression and a defective DNA damage response in their cells.
mod_finding: P53 KO fetuses and live piglets were delivered via caesarean section.
gest_age: 38 days (for collected fetuses); N/A for live piglets
